title: Phrasal Verbs I
description: Common two-word phrasal verbs for everyday actions. Watch which ones can be split (pick it up).

words.definition: to get out of bed after sleeping
examples: I *get up* at seven every day.
words.note: wake up = open your eyes; get up = leave the bed.

words.definition: to stop sleeping
to try to find something or someone
examples: She is *looking for* a new job.
words.note: Not separable: look for it — not "look it for".

words.definition: to take care of someone or something
examples: Can you *look after* my cat this weekend?

words.definition: to stop trying; to stop a habit
words.note: give up + -ing. Separable: give it up.

words.definition: to learn a fact or information that you did not know
examples: I need to *find out* when the train leaves.

words.definition: to start a machine or light, usually by pressing a switch
words.note: Separable: turn it on. Opposite: turn off.

words.definition: to stop a machine or light from working
to lift something from a surface; to go and get someone
to place clothes, glasses, etc. on your body
examples: She *put on* her glasses to read.
words.note: put on = the action; wear = the state. Opposite: take off.

words.definition: to remove clothes; (of a plane) to leave the ground
to return to a place
examples: He *came back* from Japan last week.

words.definition: to leave your home to do something social or fun
examples: She *goes out* with friends on Fridays.
words.note: Also: a light or fire goes out = stops burning.

words.definition: to move your body into a sitting position
to rise to your feet
examples: Everyone *stood up* when the teacher came in.
words.note: stand up FOR someone = defend them.

words.definition: to put on clothes to see if they fit or look good
to write the needed information in the spaces of a form
words.note: British English often says fill in.

words.definition: to change from a child into an adult
examples: What do you want to be when you *grow up*?

words.definition: to use all of something so that none is left
to start or arrange something; to prepare equipment for use
examples: Can you help me *set up* my new computer?

words.definition: to arrive, often late or when not expected
examples: Only five people *showed up* to the meeting.

words.definition: to search for information in a dictionary, book or online
examples: *Look up* new words in the dictionary.
words.note: Separable: look it up. That's what you're doing in this app!

words.definition: to phone someone who called you, or to phone again
examples: I'm busy now. Can I *call* you *back*?

words.definition: (of a machine) to stop working; (of a person) to start crying
examples: Our car *broke down* on the highway.

words.definition: to continue doing something
words.note: carry on + -ing / carry on WITH something.

words.definition: to arrive and register at a hotel or airport
examples: We *checked in* at the hotel at 3 p.m.
You must *check in* two hours before your flight.

words.definition: (informal) to spend time relaxing, often with friends
examples: We usually *hang out* at the park.
Do you want to *hang out* this weekend?

words.definition: to wait for a short time; to hold something tightly
examples: *Hold on* a second, I'll get my pen.

words.definition: to put something in the trash because you don't want it
examples: Don't *throw away* that box — I need it.

words.definition: to exercise; to find the answer to something; to end well
examples: I *work out* at the gym three times a week.
